rationale: Acceptance did not run (no spec) and blind/verification lenses are not part of the balanced profile; no standards coverage gap. Blocking: commit-format standards failure (ticket key in both commit subjects). 1 advisory (unbounded agent_id); 2 edge findings dismissed as already-handled (Tier B/shutdown rows are always scope main). 0 deferred.

standards_review.notes: 2 subjects use valid type, allowed scope (analytics) and are under 100 chars, but both embed the ticket key EPMCDME-16573 in the subject, which git-workflow.md Anti-Patterns lists as to avoid (reference it in the body footer instead)
1 changed file (copilot-cli-otlp.request-usage.ts): interface used for shapes, explicit return type on new helper, new function under 50 lines, why-comment present, no console.log, no any
no credentials, logging, paths or X-CodeMie-* header injection touched; agent_id is an added analytics event field built from trimmed string input only

findings.title: Commit subjects embed ticket key
findings.problem: Both commits in the review range ('feat(analytics): EPMCDME-16573 carry Copilot sub-agent id on agent.usage.request' and 'fix(analytics): EPMCDME-16573 attribute agent_id only to sub-agent requests') put the ticket key in the subject, which git-workflow.md Anti-Patterns lists as to avoid.
findings.impact: Documented commit-format convention is broken in every commit of the review range; blocks the workflow.
findings.recommendation: Reword both commits to '<type>(analytics): <subject>' without the ticket key and add 'EPMCDME-16573' in the body footer.

findings.title: Sub-agent id copied unbounded
findings.problem: recordAgentId trims but does not length-bound or sanitize the Copilot-supplied agentId before it is written to agent_id.
findings.impact: Only a pathological or hostile Copilot event stream triggers it; the value is analytics-only metadata, so the consequence is an oversized row. Reachability of an oversized id not confirmed.
findings.recommendation: Cap length, e.g. candidate.trim().slice(0, 128), matching the hook path's bounding.
